agenda_text:
This Agenda contains a brief general description of each item to be considered. Copies of the Staff reports or
 other written documentation relating to each item of business referred to on the Agenda are on file in the Office
 of the City Clerk and are available for public inspection. Any person who has a question concerning any of the
 agenda items may call the City Manager at (310) 603-0220, ext. 200.

  Procedures for Addressing the Council

 IN ORDER TO EXPEDITE CITY COUNCIL BUSINESS, WE ASK THAT ALL PERSONS WISHING TO
 ADDRESS  THE  COUNCIL  SUBMIT  YOUR  COMMENTS  IN  ADVANCE  TO
 CITYCLERK@LYNWOODCA.GOV OR FILL OUT A FORM PROVIDED AT THE PODIUM, AND TO TURN IT
 IN TO THE CITY CLERK PRIOR TO THE START OF THE MEETING. FAILURE TO FILL OUT SUCH A
 FORM WILL PROHIBIT YOU FROM ADDRESSING THE COUNCIL IN THE ABSENCE OF THE
 UNANIMOUS CONSENT OF THE COUNCIL.

  AGENDA
  City Council Regular Meeting
  TO BE HELD ON

  December 17, 2024

  COUNCIL CHAMBERS - 11350 BULLIS ROAD. LYNWOOD, CA 90262
  Duly Posted on 12/13/24 By CO for MQ
  6:00 PM

  PUBLIC ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

  NON-AGENDA PUBLIC ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

 THIS PORTION PROVIDES AN OPPORTUNITY FOR THE PUBLIC TO ADDRESS THE
 COUNCIL ON ITEMS WITHIN THE JURISDICTION OF THE COUNCIL AND NOT LISTED
 ON THE AGENDA. IF AN ITEM IS NOT ON THE AGENDA, THERE SHOULD BE NO
 SUBSTANTIAL DISCUSSION OF THE ISSUE BY THE COUNCIL, BUT COUNCIL MAY
 REFER THE MATTER TO STAFF OR SCHEDULE SUBSTANTIVE DISCUSSION FOR A
 FUTURE MEETING. (The Ralph M. Brown Act, Government Code Section 54954.2 (a).)

 8. CONSENT CALENDAR
 ALL MATTERS LISTED UNDER THE CONSENT CALENDAR WILL BE ACTED UPON BY
 ONE MOTION AFFIRMING THE ACTION RECOMMENDED ON THE AGENDA. THERE
 WILL BE NO SEPARATE DISCUSSION ON THESE ITEMS PRIOR TO VOTING UNLESS
 MEMBERS OF THE COUNCIL OR STAFF REQUEST SPECIFIC ITEMS TO BE REMOVED
 FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR FOR SEPARATE ACTION.

 8.1 APPROVAL OF THE WARRANT REGISTER
  Comments:
  City of Lynwood warrant register dated December 17, 2024 for FY 2024-2025. (FIN)

  Recommendation:
  Staff respectfully recommends that the City Council of the City of Lynwood approve the
  warrant register dated December 17, 2024 for FY 2024-2025.

 8.2 PREVIOUS MEETING MINUTES
  Comments:
  The purpose of this item is to have the Lynwood City Council review and approve the City
  Council meeting action minutes. (CC)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the Lynwood City Council approve the following meeting action
  minutes:
  November 19, 2024 Regular Meeting and Closed Session Regular Meeting Action
  Minutes
  December 3, 2024 Regular Meeting Action Minutes

 8.3 SCHEDULING CANCELATION OF FUTURE CITY COUNCIL MEETING

City Council Regular Meeting
  2
   Comments:
  City Council to consider declaring dark on January 7th, the first City Council meeting of
  2025. (CM)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council cancel and declare dark the first meeting in
  January.

 8.4 CERTIFICATION, REVIEW, AND GRANTING OF UTILITY USER'S TAX EXEMPTIONS
  FOR CALENDAR YEAR 2025
  Comments:
  In November 1990, the City Council adopted Ordinance No. 1352 establishing a Utility
  User's Tax on water, electricity, gas, and telephone services. In addition, the City Council
  adopted Resolution No. 90 -191 (Exhibit " A"), implementing a schedule for levying the
  Utility User's Tax and establishing certain exemptions from the Tax. Section 5, Resolution
  No. 90-191, states that the Tax Administrator for the City, currently the Director of
  Finance & Administration, shall review and certify the eligibility of each applicant for
  waiver of the Utility Users' Tax. All certifications also require City Council approval. On
  November 4, 2008, voters approved and ratified the City's Utility User's Tax (UUT) at a
  reduced rate of 9% from the previous rate of 10%. The voters also approved the update of
  the City's Ordinance based on changes in laws and technology that occurred since 1990.
  However, the existing exemptions were maintained. (FIN)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council review and approve the attached resolution
  entitled: "A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD
  APPROVING THE CERTIFIED LIST OF UTILITY USER'S TAX EXEMPTIONS FOR THE
  PERIOD OF JANUARY 1, 2025 THROUGH DECEMBER 31, 2025, AND GRANTING
  EXEMPTIONS TO THE INDIVIDUALS ON THE CERTIFIED LISTS."

 8.5 PROJECT ACCEPTANCE FOR THE EMERGENCY GENERATOR AND SITE
  IMPROVEMENTS PROJECT (WELL NO.8) CIP PROJECT NO. 4011.67.901
  Comments:

  The City of Lynwood awarded a construction contract to R2BUILD dba R2B
  ENGINEERING on December 17, 2019, for the Emergency Generator and Site
  Improvements Project (Well No.8) CIP Project No. 4011.67.901. The project has since
  been completed and is ready for acceptance by the City Council. (PW)

  Recommendation:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the attached resolution entitled: “A
  RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD ACCEPTING
  THE EMERGENCY GENERATOR AND SITE IMPROVEMENTS PROJECT (WELL
  NO.8) CIP PROJECT NO. 4011.67.901 AS COMPLETE; AUTHORIZING THE FILING OF

City Council Regular Meeting
  3
   THE NOTICE OF COMPLETION WITH THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY RECORDER’S
  OFFICE AND THE RELEASE OF THE 5% RETENTION 35 DAYS AFTER THE
  ACCEPTANCE.”

 8.6 PROJECT ACCEPTANCE FOR THE WATER MAIN REPLACEMENT PROJECT FOR
  FY 2024 CIP PROJECT NO. 4011.68.134
  Comments:

  The City of Lynwood awarded a construction contract to Dominguez General
  Engineering, Inc. on September 5, 2023, for the Water Main Replacement Project for FY
  2024 California Avenue, Fernwood Avenue, and Santa Fe Avenue Project, CIP Project
  No. 4011.68.134. The project has been completed and is now ready for acceptance by
  the City Council. (PW)

  Recommendation:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the attached resolution entitled: “A
  RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD ACCEPTING
  THE WATER MAIN REPLACEMENT Project for FY 2024 CIP PROJECT NO.
  4011.68.134 AS COMPLETE; AUTHORIZING THE FILING OF THE NOTICE OF
  COMPLETION WITH THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY RECORDER’S OFFICE AND THE
  RELEASE OF THE 5% RETENTION 35 DAYS AFTER THE ACCEPTANCE.”

 8.7 REJECTION OF BID FOR THE WATER DIVISION OFFICE IMPROVEMENTS PHASE 1
  PROJECT CIP NO. 4011.67.928
  Comments:

  As part of the Fiscal Year (FY) 2023-2024 budget, an improvement project for the Water
  Division's office at the City of Lynwood Public Works Yard was planned. After an
  extensive bidding process, only one bid was received, but it came in significantly over
  budget. As a result, staff is recommending that City Council reject the bid and reevaluate
  the project's plans, specifications, and funding before rebidding to ensure the project
  aligns with the budget. (PW)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the attached resolution entitled: “A
  RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD REJECTING THE
  BID FOR THE WATER DIVISION OFFICE IMPROVEMENTS PHASE 1 PROJECT CIP
  NO. 4011.67.928.”

 8.8 AWARD OF CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT TO ALL AMERICAN ASPHALT FOR THE
  AGNES STRIPING PROJECT, FY 2024-2025 (CIP PROJECT NO. 2350|2352.68.145)
  Comments:

City Council Regular Meeting
  4
   On November 13, 2024, staff solicited bids for construction of the Agnes Striping Project.
  On November 26, 2024 staff received three (3) bids for the Project. Upon review of bids,
  staff recommends that the City Council award the contract to All American Asphalt in the
  amount of $189,568.00. (PW)

  Recommendation:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the attached resolution entitled: “A
  RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD AWARDING a
  CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT TO ALL AMERICAN ASPHALT FOR THE AGNES
  STRIPING PROJECT, FY 2024-2025 (CIP PROJECT NO. 2350|2352.68.145).”

 8.9
  AWARD OF CONTRACT TO GENTRY GENERAL ENGINEERING, INC. FOR THE
  SIDEWALK IMPROVEMENT PROJECT, FY 2024-2025 (CIP PROJECT NOS.
  2121|2251.68.143 & 4011.68.130)

  Comments:

  Staff sent an informal request for proposal to six contractors for the Annual Sidewalk
  Improvement Project Fiscal Year (FY) 25. After review, staff recommends that the City
  Council award the construction contract to Gentry General Engineering Inc. for an amount
  of $117,238.00. (PW)

  Recommendation:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the attached resolution entitled: “A
  RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD AWARDING a
  CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT TO GENTRY GENERAL ENGINEERING, INC. FOR THE
  SIDEWALK IMPROVEMENT PROJECT, FY 2024-2025 (CIP PROJECT NOS.
  2121|2251.68.145 & 4011.68.130)”

 8.10 APPROVAL OF CONTINGENCY INCREASE FOR THE IMPERIAL HIGHWAY
  CORRIDOR CAPACITY ENHANCEMENT PROJECT FROM STATE STREET TO
  WRIGHT ROAD FY 2023-2024, PROJECT NO. 4011.68.106
  Comments:

  On March 15, 2023, the City of Lynwood and the Los Angeles County Metropolitan
  Transportation Authority (LACMTA) entered into an agreement for improvements along
  Imperial Highway to enhance capacity. On August 15, 2023, the City Council awarded a
  contract to All American Asphalt for the construction of the Imperial Highway Capacity
  Enhancement Project. As work has progressed, unforeseen circumstances have led to
  the need for change orders. Staff is now requesting approval for an increase in the project
  contingency. (PW)

City Council Regular Meeting
  5
   Recommendation:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the attached resolution entitled: “A
  RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD APPROVING A
  CONTINGENCY INCREASE FOR THE IMPERIAL HIGHWAY CORRIDOR CAPACITY
  ENHANCEMENT PROJECT FROM STATE STREET TO WRIGHT ROAD FY 2023-2024,
  PROJECT NO. 4011.68.106”

 8.11
  APPROVAL OF SIXTH AMENDMENT TO CONTRACT WITH WATERWORKS
  TECHNOLOGY, INC. FOR CONTINUING TO PROVIDE INTERIM MANAGEMENT OF
  THE WATER AND SEWER OPERATIONS AND CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROJECTS
  FOR THE CITY’S PUBLIC WORKS DEPARTMENT

  Comments:
  The City’s existing agreement with Waterworks Technology, Inc. is set to expire on
  December 31, 2024. Staff is working on awarding a new contract for utility support
  services. As the expiration of the existing contract is near, Staff is recommending to City
  Council to approve an amendment to the existing agreement with Waterworks
  Technology, Inc. to continue to provide Professional Utility Support services for up to one
  (1) additional year. (PW)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the attached resolution entitled: “A
  RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD APPROVING A
  SIXTH AMENDMENT TO THE AGREEMENT WITH WATERWORKS TECHNOLOGY,
  INC. FOR THE INTERIM MANAGEMENT OF THE WATER AND SEWER OPERATIONS
  AND CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROJECTS; AUTHORIZING THE CITY MANAGER TO
  APPROVE AGREEMENT AMENDMENTS RELATED TO THE AGREEMENT”.

 8.12
  APPROVAL TO VACATE A PORTION OF FERNWOOD AVENUE BETWEEN
  ALAMEDA STREET AND IMPERIAL HIGHWAY

  Comments:

  Staff is looking to develop City owned lots that are located along Fernwood Avenue
  between Imperial Highway and Alameda Street. A section of Fernwood Avenue is
  currently not in use and will interfere with the future development of residential and
  commercial properties on the lots. Staff is recommending City Council approve the street
  vacation of the portion of Fernwood Avenue between Alameda Street and Imperial
  Highway. (PW)

  Recommendation:

City Council Regular Meeting
  6
   Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the attached resolution entitled: “A
  RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD DETERMINING
  THAT THE VACATION OF A PORTION OF FERNWOOD AVENUE FROM 795 FEET
  SOUTHEAST OF ALAMEDA STREET TO IMPERIAL HIGHWAY IS IN CONFORMANCE
  WITH THE ADOPTED GENERAL PLAN OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD AND ORDERING
  THE VACATION OF THAT PORTION OF FERNWOOD AVENUE.”

 9.  NEW/OLD BUSINESS

 9.1
  FISCAL YEAR (FY) 2024-25 MID-YEAR FINANCIAL REVIEW

  Comments:

  The Fiscal Year (FY) 2024-25 Mid-Year Financial Review reports on the City’s fiscal
  performance through mid-year (July through December), comparing all revenues and
  expenditures incurred during the first two quarters of FY 2024-25 to the same period in FY
  2023-24. The Mid-Year Financial Review also provides an updated FY 2024-25 Financial
  Forecast, as well as presents mid-year budget adjustments for Council’s consideration to
  amend the FY 2024-25 Adopted Budget. (FIN)

  Recommendation:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the attached resolution entitled, “A
  RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD RECEIVING AND
  FILING THE FY 2024-25 MID-YEAR FINANCIAL REVIEW, APPROVING THE FY 2024-
  25 MID-YEAR BUDGET ADJUSTMENTS TO AMEND THE FY 2024-25 ADOPTED
  BUDGET HERETO ATTACHED AS SCHEDULE A”.

 9.2 SELECTION AND APPROVAL OF SECURITY SERVICES PROVIDER FOR THE
  CITY'S PARKS AND FACILITIES
  Comments:
  On August 7, 2024 staff issued a Request for Proposals (RFP) to solicit qualified security
  firms to provide proposals for Security Guard Services for the City’s parks and public
  facilities. The RFP process has concluded, staff has prepared a list of ranked firms and is
  making a selection recommendation for City Council consideration. (REC)

  Recommendation:

  Staff recommends that the City Council review the list of qualified security firms, consider
  the information provided within the staff report and:

  1. Approve the award of a two-year contract for security services to American Guard

City Council Regular Meeting
  7
   Services, Inc. with options for three one-year terms, for an estimated annual cost of
  $556,000;

  AND

  2.Adopt the attached resolution entitled, “A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF
  THE CITY OF LYNWOOD AUTHORIZING THE MAYOR TO EXECUTE AN
  AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE CITY OF LYNWOOD AND AMERICAN GUARD
  SERVICES , INC. TO PROVIDE SECURITY GUARD SERVICES FOR THE CITY OF
  LYNWOOD’S PARKS AND PUBLIC FACILITIES.”

 9.3 SECOND AMENDMENT TO THE LYNWOOD DIAL-A-TAXI AGREEMENT
  Comments:
  For over the past 25 years, the City of Lynwood has offered an on-demand (Dial-a-
  Ride/Taxi) transportation program to help serve the needs of Lynwood seniors and
  residents with disabilities. The service is provided to senior citizens and disabled
  residents for medical appointments, grocery shopping, and participation in Senior Center
  activities. Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the accompanying resolution
  approving a Second Amendment and extending the term of the agreement through
  December 18, 2025. (REC)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the attached resolution entitled; “ A
  RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD APPROVING
  THE SECOND AMENDMENT TO THE LYNWOOD DIAL-A-TAXI CONTRACT WITH
  FIESTA TAXI COOPERATIVE, INC., AND AUTHORIZING THE MAYOR TO EXECUTE
  THE SECOND AMENDMENT EXTENDING THE TERM OF THE AGREEMENT
  THROUGH DECEMBER 18, 2025, FOR A NOT-TO-EXCEED AMOUNT OF $200,000 .”

 9.4 MAYORAL APPOINTMENTS
  Comments:
  Members of the City Council serve on various municipal organizations that require
  representation of government officers. This participation allows the City to receive
  beneficial information and resources. Previously, the Mayor has made appointments to
  the organizations, with approval and ratification of members of the City Council. As a
  result of the City Council's recent reorganization, the Mayor and Council will review and
  update the list of appointments accordingly. (CC)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the Mayor and Council review and appoint delegates and
  alternates for the various organizations and committees, and direct staff to notify said
  organizations on the appointments.

City Council Regular Meeting
  8
  9.5 REVIEW OF BOARD, COMMISSION AND COMMITTEE MEMBERS & ANNUAL
  BOARDS, COMMISSIONS AND COMMITTEES LOCAL APPOINTMENT LIST
  Comments:
  Review of Board and Commission Members & Annual Boards and Commissions Local
  Appointment List. (CC)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council review the list of Board and Commission
  members. In accordance with the rules outlined below, the City Council may make any
  adjustments to these Boards and Commissions, as it deems appropriate.

  Additionally, staff recommends that the City Council direct staff to post the attached
  annual City of Lynwood Boards and Commission Appointment List pursuant to
  Government Code Section 54970 requirements.

 10. CITY COUNCIL ORAL AND WRITTEN COMMUNICATION

 11. STAFF ORAL COMMENTS

  ADJOURNMENT

 THE NEXT REGULAR MEETING WILL BE HELD ON JANUARY 21, 2025 AT 6:00 P.M. IN
 THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS OF THE CITY HALL ANNEX, 11350 BULLIS ROAD, CITY OF
 LYNWOOD, CALIFORNIA.

 SUBJECT:  CERTIFICATION, REVIEW, AND GRANTING OF UTILITY USER'S TAX
  EXEMPTIONS FOR CALENDAR YEAR 2025

 Recommendation:

 Staff recommends that the City Council review and approve the attached resolution entitled: "A
 RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD APPROVING THE
 CERTIFIED LIST OF UTILITY USER'S TAX EXEMPTIONS FOR THE PERIOD OF JANUARY
 1, 2025 THROUGH DECEMBER 31, 2025, AND GRANTING EXEMPTIONS TO THE
 INDIVIDUALS ON THE CERTIFIED LISTS."

 Background:

 In November 1990, the City Council adopted Ordinance No. 1352 establishing a Utility User's
 Tax on water, electricity, gas, and telephone services. In addition, the City Council adopted
 Resolution No. 90-191 ( Exhibit " A"), implementing a schedule for levying the Utility User's
 Tax and establishing certain exemptions from the Tax. Section 5, Resolution No. 90-191,
 states that the Tax Administrator for the City, currently the Director of Finance &
 Administration, shall review and certify the eligibility of each applicant for waiver of the Utility
 User's Tax. All certifications also require City Council approval.

 The criteria for exemption areas follows:
 a. Senior citizen status - 65 years of age or older.
 b. Use of Cogeneration (any technology for providing energy will be exempt from Utility User's
 Tax for portion of power produced cogeneration).
 c. Cable TV Service
 d. Permanently Disabled Lynwood Residents (in September 1999, City Council approved and
 adopted Resolution 99-154 (Exhibit "B) exempting the permanently disabled from the Utility
 User's Tax)

City Council City Council Regular Meeting
  48
  To date, no exemptions have been given for employing cogeneration technology. However, for
 the period of January 1 through December 31, 2025, one hundred and thirty-two (132) senior
 citizens and six (6) permanently disabled residents for the total of one hundred thirty-eight
 (138) residents have been certified by the Director of Finance & Administration or designated
 staff. Cable TV services are exempted as a group and are not separately identified on the
 certification.

 Discussion and Analysis:

 Exhibit "C" of the attached Resolution provides for the City Council's review and approval of
 the names of 138 residents certified for Utility User's Tax exemptions for the period of January
 1, 2025 through December 31 2025. Staff have reviewed and determined that all applicants
 on Exhibit "C" of the attached Resolution have met the criteria for exemption as established by
 Resolution No.90-191and No. 99-154.

 Fiscal Impact:

 The estimated loss of revenue from the above exemptions is $45,690 for the period of January
 1, 2025 through December 31, 2025. There is no impact in the FY 25 Adopted Budget.

TO THE UTILITY  USERS'  TAX

  WHEREAS, on November 4, 2008 voters approved and ratified the City' s Utility
User' Tax ( UUT) at a reduced rate of 9 %; and

  WHEREAS, the voters also approved updating the City' s UUT ordinance based
on changes in laws and technology that had occurred since 1990; and

  WHEREAS, the City Council seeks to clarify the exceptions to Telephone Users'
Tax to ensure that the UUT' s applicability is consistent with the intent of the ordinance
approved by the voters; and  t

  WHEREAS, the City Council seeks to add a section to the Telephone Users' Tax
to clarify the Tax Administrator' s authority to administer administrative rulings to
implement the Telephone Users' Tax; and

  WHEREAS, the City Council seeks to amend its UUT ordinance to clarify the
refunds procedure including the statute of limitations.

  NOW THEREFORE, THE CITY COUNCIL  OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD  DOES
HEREBY ORDAIN AS FOLLOWS:

  Section  1.  Section 6 -5. 5 of Chapter 6 of the Lynwood Municipal Code is
hereby amended to read in its entirety as follows:

6 -5. 5 Telephone Users Tax.

a.
  There is hereby imposed a tax on the amounts paid for any intrastate or
  interstate telephone communication services by every person in the City using
  such services including commercial mobile radio services. The tax imposed by
  this subsection  shall be at the rate of not more than nine ( 9 %) percent  of the
  charges made for such services and shall be paid by the person paying for such
  services.

b.  As  used  in this  subsection,  the  term "  charges"  shall not include charges for
  services paid for by inserting coins in coin -operated telephones except that
  where  such  coin - operated  service  is furnished  for a guaranteed  amount,  the
  amounts paid under such guarantee plus any fixed monthly or other periodic
  charge shall be included in the base for computing the amount of tax due; nor
  shall the term " charges" include charges for any type of service or equipment

  furnished by a service supplied subject to public utility regulations during any
  period in which the same or similar services  or equipment  are also available for
  sale or lease from persons other than a service supplier subject to public utility
  regulation;  nor  shall  the  words " telephone  communication  services"  include

   maritime mobile services as defined in Section 2. 1 of Title 47 of the Code of
  Federal  Regulations,  as said section existed on January 1,  1970.  The term
  telephone  communication  services"  refers  to  that  services  which  provides
  access  to  a  telephone  system  and  the  privilege  of  telephone  quality
  communication with substantially all persons having telephone stations which are
  part of such telephone  system.  The Telephone  Users'  Tax is intended  to, and
  does, apply to all charges billed to a telephone account having a situs in the City,
  irrespective  of whether  a particular  communication  service  originates  and /or
  terminates within the City.

C.
  The tax imposed by this subsection shall be collected from the service user by
  the  person  providing  the  intrastate  or  interstate  telephone  communication
  services, or the person receiving payment for such services. The amount of the
  tax collected  in one ( 1)  month shall be remitted to the Tax Administrator on or
  before the last day of the following month; or at the option of the person required
  to collect and remit the tax, an estimated amount of tax collected, measured by
  the tax bill in the previous month, shall be remitted. to the Tax Administrator on or
  before the last day of each month.

d.  The Tax Administrator may issue and disseminate to telephone communication
  service suppliers, which are subject to the tax collection  requirements  of this
  Chapter, an administrative ruling:  i) identifying those telephone communication
  services,  or charges therefore,  that are subject to or not subject to the tax of
  subsection ( a) above, and in rendering such a ruling, the Tax Administrator may
  consider  the  common  rules,
  guidelines and definitions promulgated by other
  taxing jurisdictions in California that impose a tax on intrastate and interstate
  telephone communications services; and, ii) establishing sourcing rules for the
  taxation  of telephone  communication  services, including but not limited to,
  commercial  mobile  radio  service,  post -paid  telephone  communication  services,
  prepaid telephone communication  services, and VoIP; provided that such rules
  are  based  upon  custom  and  common  practice  that  further  administrative
  efficiency and minimize multi -jurisdictional taxation.

e.  Notwithstanding the provisions of paragraph a., the tax imposed under this
  subsection shall not be imposed upon any person for using intrastate or
  interstate  telephone  communication  services to the extent that the amounts  paid
  for such services are exempt from the tax imposed under Division 2, Part 20 of
  the California  Revenue  and Taxation  Code, or the tax imposed  under Section
  4251  of the Internal  Revenue  Code.

 SUBJECT:  PROJECT ACCEPTANCE FOR THE EMERGENCY GENERATOR AND
  SITE IMPROVEMENTS PROJECT (WELL NO.8) CIP PROJECT NO.
  4011.67.901

 Recommendation:

 Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the attached resolution entitled: “A
 RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD ACCEPTING THE
 EMERGENCY GENERATOR AND SITE IMPROVEMENTS PROJECT (WELL NO.8) CIP
 PROJECT NO. 4011.67.901 AS COMPLETE; AUTHORIZING THE FILING OF THE NOTICE
 OF COMPLETION WITH THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY RECORDER’S OFFICE AND THE
 RELEASE OF THE 5% RETENTION 35 DAYS AFTER THE ACCEPTANCE.”

 Background:

 In 2019, the City Council approved the installation of generators at well sites and the Booster
 Pump Station. Staff chose to phase out the project due to its complexity. The Emergency
 Generator & Site Improvements Project was designated as Phase 1, and the project analysis
 and facility testing from this phase were documented and incorporated into the subsequent
 phases of the project.

 The Notice Inviting Bids was published in the Daily Journal, Dodge, Analytical, Bid America,
 and on the City’s website (PlanetBids) on October 16, 2019. The bid opening occurred on the
 PlanetBids platform on November 21, 2019 at 1:00 P.M.

City Council City Council Regular Meeting
  68
  Discussion and Analysis:

 On December 17, 2019, the City awarded the contract to the lowest responsible bidder, R2B
 Engineering in the amount of $824,000. A Notice to Proceed was issued, marking the start of
 construction on February 10, 2020. Throughout the project, ten (10) change orders were
 issued. The final date of construction was in April 2021.

 Scope of Work:

 The work performed included the construction of a generator and control building, including
 installation of lighting, an exhaust system, HVAC, fire sprinklers, and the owner-furnished
 engine generator. Additional work involved constructing electrical control panels, including the
 Well No. 8 VFD, automatic transfer station, conduits, and electrical panels; linking the
 automatic transfer station to Well No. 8 and booster stations; and removing and disposing of
 existing concrete and/or asphalt, station improvements, trees, light post, hedges, shrubs,
 vines, piping, conduits, and other elements interfering with the new improvements. Site
 improvements included constructing a perimeter site wall, concrete pathways, landscaping,
 relocating light poles and conduits, and an irrigation system. The work was performed at the
 Well No. 8 site, located at 11331 Bullis Road, Lynwood, California 90262.

 Approved Budget:

 The original contract amount with R2B Engineering was $824,000. During construction, staff
 made several field adjustments to address discrepancies in working conditions, resulting in ten
 (10) change orders totaling a revised contract amount of $1,001,185.73.

 Additionally, $123,924.00 was allocated for construction management and inspection services,
 while $21,400 was used for labor compliance tasks performed by Avant Garde Inc. Staff time,
 construction support, and other related project management costs totaled $102,046.11.

 SUBJECT:  PROJECT ACCEPTANCE FOR THE WATER MAIN REPLACEMENT
  PROJECT FOR FY 2024 CIP PROJECT NO. 4011.68.134

 Recommendation:

 Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the attached resolution entitled: “A
 RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD ACCEPTING THE
 WATER MAIN REPLACEMENT Project for FY 2024 CIP PROJECT NO. 4011.68.134 AS
 COMPLETE; AUTHORIZING THE FILING OF THE NOTICE OF COMPLETION WITH THE
 LOS ANGELES COUNTY RECORDER’S OFFICE AND THE RELEASE OF THE 5%
 RETENTION 35 DAYS AFTER THE ACCEPTANCE.”

 Background:

 As part of the City of Lynwood's five-year Capital Improvement Program (CIP), the City
 requested the design for water main replacement and upgrades at multiple locations.

 On July 18, 2023, the City Council approved the plans and specifications and authorized the
 bidding process for the project. The Notice Inviting Bids was uploaded to the City’s website
 (PlanetBids) on July 20, 2023. The bid opening occurred on Monday, August 21, 2023, at
 10:00 A.M.

 Discussion and Analysis:

City Council City Council Regular Meeting
  75
  On September 5, 2023, the City awarded the contract to the lowest responsible bidder,
 Dominguez General Engineering, Inc. in the amount of $1,065,380.00. A Notice to Proceed
 was issued, marking the start of construction on January 8, 2024. Throughout the project, one
 (1) change order was issued. The final date of construction was July 8, 2024.

 Scope of Work:

 The work performed consisted of water main installation, water main replacement, temporary
 highlining, fire hydrants, water service, pavement restoration, and partial replacement of
 concrete sidewalks, curb and gutters, and driveways approaches.

 The project limits for the improvements were Santa Fe Avenue from 108th Street to 109th
 Street, California Avenue from Martin Luther King Jr. Boulevard. to 200 South of Martin Luther
 King Jr. Boulevard, Fernwood Avenue from Atlantic Avenue to Virginia Avenue, Fernwood
 Avenue from Muriel Drive to Harris Avenue and the alleys located east and west of Thorson
 Avenue by Fernwood Avenue.

 Approved Budget:

 The original contract amount with Dominguez General Engineering, Inc. was $1,065,380.00.
 During construction, staff made a field adjustment to address discrepancies in the design

 Background:

 On July 7, 2020, the City Council awarded a construction contract for improvements to Agnes

 This project featured new striping from Bullis Road to Atlantic Avenue, with parking brackets
 on both sides and a center median approximately thirty feet wide from Thorson Avenue to
 Atlantic Avenue. The project was accepted as complete on April 5, 2022.

 Since its completion, concerns have risen regarding the striping. Issues include vehicles using
 the center median as a travel lane and the placement of trash bins in that area. Additionally,
 the number of installed parking T's has been inadequate for local residents. In response to
 these concerns, staff requested that the on-call consultant Transtech Engineers Inc. create a
 new striping design for Agnes Avenue from Thorson Avenue to Atlantic Avenue. The
 redesigned layout aims to increase parking capacity and improve safety for drivers. This
 updated striping design was completed and approved by the City Council on September 17,

 RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD AWARDING a
 CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT TO GENTRY GENERAL ENGINEERING, INC. FOR THE
 SIDEWALK IMPROVEMENT PROJECT, FY 2024-2025 (CIP PROJECT NOS.
 2121|2251.68.145 & 4011.68.130)”

 Background:

 Sidewalk improvements are implemented as part of the City's 5-year Capital Improvement
 Project (CIP) program. These improvements are crucial because they enhance pedestrian
 safety, provide better accessibility for people with disabilities, reduce the risk of accidents, and
 promote overall walkability within the community. Additionally, well-maintained sidewalks
 contribute to the aesthetic appeal of neighborhoods and can encourage healthier, more
 sustainable modes of transportation.

 Staff conducted an Informal Request for Proposals (IRFP) for the Sidewalk Improvements
 Project Fiscal Year (FY) 24-25 CIP No. 2121|2251.68.145 & 4011.68.130. Per the City’s
 Contracting and Purchasing Policy and Procedures Section XII, staff can move forward with

 issued to obtain written, competitive proposals to be used as a basis for entering a contract
 when price will not necessarily be the predominant award criteria.

 Recommendation:

 Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the attached resolution entitled: “A
 RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD APPROVING A SIXTH
 AMENDMENT TO THE AGREEMENT WITH WATERWORKS TECHNOLOGY, INC. FOR
 THE INTERIM MANAGEMENT OF THE WATER AND SEWER OPERATIONS AND CAPITAL
 IMPROVEMENT PROJECTS; AUTHORIZING THE CITY MANAGER TO APPROVE
 AGREEMENT AMENDMENTS RELATED TO THE AGREEMENT”.

 Background:

 The City provides water service to approximately 69,900 residents, through about 9,620 water
 services utilizing 95 miles of water distribution pipelines and one (1) reservoir and booster
 station. The City’s water supply consists of a mix of local groundwater and imported water.
 The City pumps groundwater from the Central Groundwater Basin, in conjunction with the
 Water Replenishment District of Southern California (WRD) through five (5) active wells that
 are owned and operated by the City. Imported water is sourced from Metropolitan Water
 District (MWD) via Central Basin Municipal Water District (CBMWD).

 The City of Lynwood’s Utilities Division operates and oversees the City’s water and sewer
 collection systems including maintaining the water supply, ensuring water quality, maintaining,
 and upgrading the water system and sewer collection system infrastructure and providing
 emergency response. In order to continue to provide utility services to the Lynwood residents,
 the City requires the assistance of a consultant company to provide utility support services. On

City Council City Council Regular Meeting
  168
  September 17, 2024 the City Council approved an amendment to the existing agreement with
 Waterworks Technology, Inc. to extend the contract to December 31, 2024.

 Discussion and Analysis:

 Waterworks Technology, Inc. has been providing staffing necessary to manage the water and
 sewer systems as well as submit the necessary reports to various State agencies overseeing
 drinking water quality and production. Waterworks Technology, Inc. has also assisted staff
 with the on-going CIPs. Currently, Waterworks Technology, Inc. provides the required
 certification to manage the City’s water system, classified as a D5 Distribution System and
 provides 24/7 stand-by chief operator and reported as such to the State Water Resources
 Control Board.

 WaterWorks Technology Inc’s current contract provides service to the City under the same
 terms of the original contract. As the existing contract is set to expire on December 31, 2024,
 Staff scheduled to award a 3-year contract for Utility Support and Management Services on
 November 19, 2024. However, the City received a formal protest letter on November 19,2024.
 Staff will require additional time to fully consider the claims in the protest.

 The City’s Contracting and Purchasing Policy allows three (3) amendments to the original
 contract. However an exception to this policy is allowed for emergency or urgent need of
 services to ensure the continuation of the City operations. An amendment to the existing
 contract, extending the term to up to December 31, 2025 is needed. The additional time will
 allow Staff to fully evaluate the claims in the protest and to determine the most optimal solution
 in order for the City to have a smooth transition with no disruptions to the City’s management
 of the water and sewer systems.

 Fiscal Impact:

 The compensation for the consultant will based on their fee schedule and will be paid from the
 approved FY 24-25 and proposed FY 25-26 Water and Sewer funds. No additional
 appropriation is needed at this time.

 SUBJECT:
  APPROVAL TO VACATE A PORTION OF FERNWOOD AVENUE
  BETWEEN ALAMEDA STREET AND IMPERIAL HIGHWAY

 Recommendation:

 Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the attached resolution entitled: “A
 RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD DETERMINING THAT
 THE VACATION OF A PORTION OF FERNWOOD AVENUE FROM 795 FEET SOUTHEAST
 OF ALAMEDA STREET TO IMPERIAL HIGHWAY IS IN CONFORMANCE WITH THE
 ADOPTED GENERAL PLAN OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD AND ORDERING THE
 VACATION OF THAT PORTION OF FERNWOOD AVENUE.”

 Background:

 The City of Lynwood is planning the development of affordable housing and commercial
 development on the City owned Alameda Triangle properties. The Triangle properties are
 three parcels known as Assessor Parcel Numbers 6169-002-904 (now 6169-002-912), 6169-
 002-905 (now 6169-002-912) and 6169-001-900. The parcels are split between north and
 south Fernwood Avenue as shown on Los Angeles County Assessor’s map (attached). In
 order to continue with the development of these properties, the City must vacate a portion of
 Fernwood Avenue located between Imperial Highway and approximately 795 feet southeast of
 Alameda Street.

 Discussion and Analysis:

City Council City Council Regular Meeting
  177
  On August 20, 2024, the City Council of the City of Lynwood adopted a resolution declaring its
 intention to vacate the aforementioned portion of Fernwood Avenue. The request is for a
 partial street vacation that will result in the vacated street to be incorporated into the
 commercial development (as shown on Attachment A). Staff reviewed the existing conditions
 of the street and has determined that the street has not been in circulation for public use as it
 has been closed from both direction of travel and is not needed for traffic circulation purposes.
  Staff has determined that it is in the public’s best interest to vacate a portion of said street.
 The design of the remaining street will comply with all fire department requirements and will
 have future access agreements through the commercial project preventing a dead-end
 condition.

 The next steps of the street vacation process are for the City to setup a Public Hearing
 meeting to discuss with all the affected and interested parties for this vacation. However, Per
 the California Streets and Highways Code (SHC) section 8334(a), the City of Lynwood may
 summarily vacate a street section if said street section is an excess right-of-way of a street or
 highway not required for street or highway purposes. As well, there are no public facilities that
 are in use and would be affected by the vacation, as required by SHC 8334.5. Additionally,
 SHC 8335 allows the City to administratively process the street vacation by adoption of a
 resolution. Therefore, staff is recommending that the City Council approve to summarily
 vacate the street section of Fernwood Avenue from approximately 795 feet southeast of
 Alameda Street to Imperial Highway.

 As required by SHC Section 8313, the City Council must consider the General Plan prior to
 vacation of a street, highway, or public service easement if the proposed vacation is within an
 area for which a General Plan has been adopted by the City. The proposed vacation is within
 the area for which the City’s General Plan has been adopted. Therefore, it is recommended
 that the City Council determine that the proposed street vacation is in conformance with the
 City’s adopted General Plan prior to ordering the vacation.

 Upon approval, staff shall cause a certified copy of this resolution to be recorded in the Los
 Angeles County Recorder’s office and upon recordation, the vacation process will be
 complete.

 Fiscal Impact:

 There is no financial impact for this item.

 Background:

 on June 26, 2024, the City Council adopted the updated second year (or FY 2024-25)

 goals, budget priorities, and desired service levels for the fiscal year, as well as identifies the
 fiscal resources necessary to achieve them. The adopted budget was based on certain
 assumptions and meeting expenditure and revenue projections.

 The FY 2024-25 Mid-Year Financial Review reports on the City’s fiscal performance through

 law enforcement, fire protection, public works services, parks, and recreation.

 closing out the year. This process includes truing up the budget, ensuring all capital

 SUBJECT:  SELECTION AND APPROVAL OF SECURITY SERVICES PROVIDER
  FOR THE CITY'S PARKS AND FACILITIES

 Recommendation:

 Staff recommends that the City Council review the list of qualified security firms, consider the
 information provided within the staff report and:

 1. Approve the award of a two-year contract for security services to American Guard Services,
 Inc. with options for three one-year terms, for an estimated annual cost of $556,000;

 AND

 2.Adopt the attached resolution entitled, “A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE
 CITY OF LYNWOOD AUTHORIZING THE MAYOR TO EXECUTE AN AGREEMENT
 BETWEEN THE CITY OF LYNWOOD AND AMERICAN GUARD SERVICES , INC. TO
 PROVIDE SECURITY GUARD SERVICES FOR THE CITY OF LYNWOOD’S PARKS AND
 PUBLIC FACILITIES.”

 Background:

 On August 7, 2024 staff issued a Request for Proposals (RFP) to solicit qualified security firms
 to provide proposals for Security Guard Services for the City’s parks and public facilities. The

City Council City Council Regular Meeting
  200
  RFP process has concluded, staff has prepared a list of ranked firms and is making a
 selection recommendation for City Council consideration.

 Discussion and Analysis:

 On August 7, 2024 the RFP was posted on the City of Lynwood’s Planet Bids vendor portal.
 The RFP was advertised on August 13, 2024 in the Press Telegram and August 15, 2024 in
 the Lynwood Press Wave. The deadline to respond to the Security RFP was September 25,
 2024.

 In time for the submittal deadline, the City received twenty-three (23) proposals. One (1) of
 the 23 proposals was determined to be incomplete, as it did not include the required six (6)
 copies of the proposal and was disqualified from consideration. Attached is the list of the
 security firms that submitted a qualifying proposal to the City. Twenty-two (22) proposals were
 evaluated by city staff management. A short-list of firms was created based on the top six (6)
 highest scoring security firms.

 The criteria used by the selection panel to evaluate the firms were developed to address the
 major consideration categories the City considers to be most relevant to the provision of cost-
 effective and high-quality security services including, but not limited to: Proposer’s operations
 approach; hiring and training programs; company experience; capacity and practical cost to
 the City.

 On November 11, 2024, the interviews were held with the six (6) short-listed firms. At the
 conclusion of the interviews, the selection panel completed their individual scoring and
 discussed the advantages and disadvantages of each firm. Individual scores were tallied and
 averaged for a final panel score. A copy of the scoring criteria used by the selection panel and
 a summary of the panelist’s scores are attached. (Attachment A).

 The selection panel scored each interview based on the following:

 its park patrol, special events and private rentals. The portion that the City spends on private

 renters of recreation facilities pay the City for required security services. The City spent
 approximately $35,000 the previous FY for security service for private facility renters.

 AGS contract and scope of work would remain essentially the same as the current level of
 service. Security services are currently contracted 365 days/year, Monday through Sunday
 from 6:30 a.m. to 10:30 p.m. AGS will provide 224 hours of security guard services weekly.
 The estimated payment to American Guard Services, Inc. would be $555,992 for the first year
 of the contract.

 If the City Council awards the contract to AGS as recommended, staff will negotiate a two-year
 agreement with an additional three, one-year options for a total possible contract term not to
 exceed five (5) years. Timing for final contract and start-up is anticipated as follows:

  Executed agreement by January 16, 2025
  Service begins under new contract February 1, 2025

 The agreement with the City’s current provider, Professional Security Consultants (PSC),
 expires on January 31, 2025.

 Staff Recommendation

  Based on a combination of the evaluation of the proposals and interviews of the top six firms,
 staff recommends that the Lynwood City Council approve the selection of American Guard
 Services as the City’s next provider of security services for protection of its parks and facilities.

 Among the six top firms, AGS ranked the highest in the interview and third in the proposal
 evaluations. The AGS submitted a consistently strong proposal primarily because of their
 operational abilities; experience, training, technological capabilities and overall average
 ranking in the review process. However, staff believes that any of top three (3) firms are
 capable of successfully providing the security services as specified in the RFP and have
 demonstrated their competence through their proposal and interview processes.

 The new contract would be for a two-year term, with options for three (3) one-year terms
 contingent upon Council approval of funding for Security Services. Based on the level of
 service, AGS would be paid an amount not-to-exceed $555,992 annually for its services for
 the first year of the agreement. The new contract commences on February 1, 2025. Under
 the terms of the new agreement included in the RFP, the firm would receive an annual rate
 increase equivalent to the increase in the Consumer Price Index, if the service contract is
 extended in years 3, 4, and 5.

 SUBJECT:  SECOND AMENDMENT TO THE LYNWOOD DIAL-A-TAXI AGREEMENT

 Recommendation:

 Staff recommends that the City Council approve the attached resolution entitled; “ A
 RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD APPROVING THE
 SECOND AMENDMENT TO THE LYNWOOD DIAL-A-TAXI CONTRACT WITH FIESTA TAXI
 COOPERATIVE, INC., AND AUTHORIZING THE MAYOR TO EXECUTE THE SECOND
 AMENDMENT EXTENDING THE TERM OF THE AGREEMENT THROUGH DECEMBER 18,
 2025, FOR A NOT-TO-EXCEED AMOUNT OF $200,000 .”

 Background:

 For over the past 25 years, the City of Lynwood has offered an on-demand (Dial-a-Ride/Taxi)
 transportation program to help serve the needs of Lynwood seniors and residents with
 disabilities. The service is provided to senior citizens and disabled residents for medical
 appointments, grocery shopping, and participation in Senior Center activities. Staff
 recommends that the City Council adopt the accompanying resolution approving a Second
 Amendment and extending the term of the agreement through December 18, 2025. (REC)

 Discussion and Analysis:

 The City’s Dial-A-Ride (DAR) program provides subsidized transportation to eligible seniors
 (65 years and older) and disabled residents living within the city limits of Lynwood. The DAR
 program is fully funded with Proposition “A” funds. The City receives an annual allocation of
 transportation grant funds for the operation of its DAR program based on historical average
 allocations. The cost of the DAR program was approximately $120,000 for FY 23/24.

 The current contract term with Fiesta Taxi to operate the City’s DAR program expires on
 December 18, 2024 (Resolution #2024.055 - First Amendment). The original agreement was

City Council City Council Regular Meeting
  215
  awarded through a formal Request for Proposals process for a contract length of five (5) years
 with a total possible value of one million dollars. A First Amendment to the agreement,
 extending the original agreement through December 18, 2024, was approved via Resolution
 #2024.055. In order to continue services, staff is now recommending approval of a Second
 Amendment to the original agreement to secure the uninterrupted continuation of a
 professional services agreement for the City's DAR program.

 If approved, the total combined cost of the first and second extensions plus the cost of the
 original 5-year agreement will still be significantly below the original approved total contract
 value of one million dollars. To date, approximately $689,000 of the originally approved one
 million dollar contract value has been expended (original cost of five years plus the cost of the
 First Amendment), leaving an approximate balance of $200,000 available to support the costs
 of the requested Second Amendment. The recommended action is in line with the City’s formal
 procedures allowed by its Contracting and Purchasing Policy & Procedures:

 Contracting and Purchasing Policy & Procedures (Section XVIII. Contract Amendments)
  “For contract amendments where the total amount of the agreement is more than
  $50,000, City Council authorization/approval is ordinarily required. A contract originally
  approved by the City Council may be amended no more than three times by the City
  Council. The term of each amendment may not exceed one year. Each amendment may
  not exceed the value of the original agreement.”

 Staff is satisfied with the services that Fiesta Taxi is providing to the City. If the Second
 Amendment is approved as recommended, it will extend the term of the Professional Services
 Agreement to December 18, 2025 .

 Fiscal Impact:

 The program cost is based on the number of trips taken; the current charge to program
 participants is $0.50 per coupon for a maximum of 18 coupons per month. Each coupon is
 good for a one-way trip. Approximately 136 active seniors receive direct transportation service
 on a monthly basis. The City currently pays Fiesta an average cost of $12.35 per trip. To date
 we are expending funds at a rate of approximately $10,400 per month for services. The
 contract amount is not-to-exceed $200,000. The recommended Second Amendment will cover
 the period of December 19, 2024 through December 18, 2025, with the funding source being
 the Proposition A Transportation Fund. Funds are included in the FY25 Adopted Budget. No
 additional funds are being requested with the recommended action.

 Fair Political Practices Commission (FPPC)

 (renumbered to 18702.5 in 2015) to allow a Public Official to participate in a decision that
 would appoint him/herself to an external board position, under a specific condition. The

 Recommendation:

 Staff recommends that the City Council, as Successor to the Lynwood Redevelopment
 Agency, adopt the attached resolution entitled: “A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF
 THE CITY OF LYNWOOD, COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES, STATE OF CALIFORNIA, AS
 SUCCESSOR TO THE LYNWOOD REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY APPROVING THE
 RECOGNIZED OBLIGATION PAYMENT SCHEDULE COVERING THE PERIOD OF JULY 1,
 2025 TO JUNE 30, 2026 AND ADOPTING THE ADMINISTRATIVE BUDGET”.

 Background:

 On June 27, 2012, the State Legislature passed AB 1484, the redevelopment budget trailer
 bill. The primary purpose of AB 1484 is to make technical and substantive amendments to
 ABx1 26. AB 1484 contains significant new requirements and harsh financial penalties on the
 Successor Agency and the City if certain provisions under AB 1484 are not carried out. Per
 Section 34177(m) of the Health and Safety Code, the Recognized Obligation Payment
 Schedule (ROPS) must be submitted by the Successor Agency, after approval by the
 oversight board, to the State Department of Finance (DOF), State Controller, County
 Administrative Officer, and the County Auditor-Controller (CAC) no later than 90 days before
 the date of property tax distribution.

Lynwood Successor Agency City of Lynwood as Successor Agency to the Lynwood Redevelopment Agency
  7
  On September 22, 2015, the Governor approved Senate Bill No. 107 (SB 107). SB 107
 makes several changes to the Redevelopment Agency (RDA) dissolution process. One of the
 key changes was changing the ROPS to an annual submittal. Pursuant to Section 34177(o)
 (1) of the Health and Safety Code, commencing with the ROPS covering the period from July
 1, 2016 to June 30, 2017, inclusive, and for each period from July 1 to June 30, inclusive
 thereafter, a Successor Agency shall submit an Oversight Board approved ROPS to the
 Department of Finance and to the County Auditor-Controller no later than February 1st of each
 year.

 Discussion and Analysis:

 ROPS

 To facilitate the payment of “enforceable obligations” a Successor Agency is required to
 prepare a ROPS. The general rule under ABx1 26 and AB 1484 is that Successor Agencies
 can only make payments on enforceable obligations listed in the ROPS by the funds identified
 in the ROPS. SB 107 expanded types of enforceable obligations that may be included in the
 ROPS.

 Enforceable obligations include, but are not limited to, the following items:

  1. Bonds;
  2. Loans or moneys borrowed by the redevelopment agency for lawful purpose;
  3. Payments required by the federal government, preexisting obligations to the State, or
  obligations imposed by state law, payments that are made by the county-auditor
  controller, or legally enforceable payments required in connection with the agencies’
  employees
  4. Judgments or settlements entered by a court or binding arbitration;
  5. Agreement or Contract entered into prior to June 28, 2011 with a third party;
  6. Contracts or agreements necessary for the administration or operation of the Successor
  Agency;
  7. Amounts borrowed from or payment owing to the Low and Moderate Income Housing
  Fund (LMIHF);
  8. Agreement between a city that created the former redevelopment agency and the former
  redevelopment agency; and
  9. Loan from the City to the Successor Agency for administrative costs, enforceable
  obligations, or project-related expenses at the city’s discretion only to the extent that the
  Successor Agency receives an insufficient distribution of Redevelopment Property Tax
  Trust Fund (RPTTF) or other approved sources are insufficient to pay approved
  enforceable obligations. Such loans placed on the ROPS reduces the Administrative
  Cost Allowance given to the Successor Agency.

Lynwood Successor Agency City of Lynwood as Successor Agency to the Lynwood Redevelopment Agency
  8
  Under SB 107, contracts or agreements between the City, County, or City and County that
 created the Redevelopment Agency can now be included. Repayments of City and former
 Agency loans will only be granted once the Successor Agency receives a Finding of
 Completion (FOC) from the DOF. On December 16, 2015, the DOF notified the City that the
 FOC had been granted.

 Administrative Budget

 Pursuant to 34177(j), a Successor Agency is required to prepare a proposed administrative
 budget and submit it to the Oversight Board for its approval. SB 107 limits the Successor
 Agency’s administrative cost allowance to an amount not to exceed 3% of the actual property
 tax distributed to the Successor Agency for payment of enforceable obligations, reduced by
 the Successor Agency’s administrative cost allowance and loan payments made to the City
 that created the Redevelopment Agency and limit a Successor Agency’s annual administrative
 costs to an amount not to exceed 50% of the total RPTTF distributed to pay enforceable
 obligations.

 Fiscal Impact:

 If a Successor Agency does not submit a ROPS by the deadline, the City that created the
 Redevelopment Agency shall be subject to a civil penalty equal to $10,000 per day for every
 day the schedule is not submitted to the DOF. Additionally, if an Agency does not submit a
 ROPS within 10 days of the deadline, the maximum administrative cost allowance for that
 period will be reduced by 25%.

 It is anticipated that the ROPS will be the basis of the distribution of tax increment by the
 County Auditor-Controller. Not receiving funding will jeopardize the Lynwood Successor
 Agency’s ability to make “enforceable obligation” payments such as the bond debt service
 payments.

A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD, COUNTY OF
LOS ANGELES, STATE OF CALIFORNIA, AS SUCCESSOR TO THE LYNWOOD
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY APPROVING THE RECOGNIZED OBLIGATION
PAYMENT SCHEDULE COVERING THE PERIOD OF JULY 1, 2025 TO JUNE 30,
2026 AND ADOPTING THE ADMINISTRATIVE BUDGET

  WHEREAS, pursuant to Section 34177(o)(1) of the Health and Safety Code,
commencing with the Recognized Obligation Payment Schedule (ROPS) covering the
period from July 1, 2016, to June 30, 2017, inclusive, and for each period from July 1 to
June 30, inclusive, thereafter, a Successor Agency shall submit an Oversight Board-
approved ROPS to the Department of Finance and to the County Auditor-Controller no
later than February 1, 2016, and each February 1 thereafter; and

  WHEREAS, pursuant to Section 34177(a)(3) of the Health and Safety Code, only
those payments listed on the ROPS may be made by the Successor Agency from the
funds specified in the ROPS; and

  WHEREAS, pursuant to Section 34177 (m)(1)(B) of the Health and Safety Code,
if the Successor Agency fails to submit a ROPS by the deadline, then the City is subject
to a civil penalty of $10,000 per day for every day the schedule is not submitted; and, in
addition, if the Successor Agency fails to submit a ROPS within 10 days of the deadline
the maximum administrative cost allowance for that period will be reduced by 25%; and

  WHEREAS, the pursuant to 34177(j) of the Health and Safety Code, a
Successor Agency is required to prepare a proposed Administrative Budget and submit
it to the Oversight Board for approval.

  NOW, THEREFORE, THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY DOES HEREBY RESOLVE
AS FOLLOWS:

  Section 1. The Recitals set forth above are true and correct and incorporated
herein by reference.

  Section 2. Approval to adopt the ROPS 25-26. The Lynwood Successor
Agency hereby authorizes staff to prepare the ROPS 25-26 covering the period of July
1, 2025 to June 30, 2026, approves the ROPS 25-26 in the form attached hereto as
Exhibit A, and to submit the completed ROPS 25-26 to the Oversight Board.

  Section 3. Authorization to Make Changes. To avoid any civil penalty that may
be imposed, the Lynwood Successor Agency authorizes the City Manager or designee
to make changes as necessary to the ROPS 25-26 before it is adopted by the Oversight
Board; and, after the ROPS 25-26 is adopted by the Oversight Board, to reflect any
changes made by the Oversight Board and to make any changes to the ROPS 25-26
thereafter, as necessary.

  18
   Section 4. Posting; Transmittal to Appropriate Agencies. The City Manager or
designee is authorized and directed to post a copy of the ROPS 25-26 on the City’s
website. The City Manager or designee is further authorized and directed to transmit,
by mail or electronic means, to the County Auditor-Controller, County Chief
Administrative Officer, the State Controller, and the State Department of Finance a copy
of the ROPS 25-26; and to respond to questions and request for documents and
information from the County and State agencies relating to the ROPS.

  Section 5. Approval to adopt the Administrative Budget. The Lynwood
Successor Agency adopts the Administrative Budget as included in the ROPS 25-26.
The City Manager or designee is authorized to submit the Administrative Budget to the
Oversight Board for approval. The City Manager or designee is authorized to make
changes to the Administrative Budget as necessary.

  Section 6. The Mayor is authorized to executed this Resolution for and on
behalf of the City of Lynwood. This Resolution shall be effective immediately upon its
adoption.

  Section 7. The City Clerk shall certify to the adoption of this Resolution and
hereafter the same shall be in full force and effect.
